evaluations.outcome: no_actionable_improvement: evaluated reusable dashboard generation across the latest 13 successful docs.yml runs from 2026-10-02T03:07Z through 2026-10-02T04:46Z and 5 comparable successful cao-dashboard.yml producer runs in the same window. Trusted docs metadata showed full workflow median 51s with p90 87s, build-job median 42s with p90 48s, schedule-freshness median 7s with p90 8s, and deploy median 17s with p90 19s on the 5 runs that actually deployed. Build-step medians remained 13s for Build documentation, 5s for Restore node_modules, 2s for Restore cached CAO Dashboard, and 10s for Upload Pages artifact. Trusted step metadata confirmed cache reuse in every sampled docs build: Install dependencies and Save node_modules were skipped, and Find latest CAO Dashboard run plus Mount latest CAO Dashboard artifact were skipped on representative docs run 36965640021 because Restore cached CAO Dashboard hit successfully. Cross-checking successful cao-dashboard runs 36962185990, 36962530424, 36963306493, 36964013511, and 36965454791 still showed the dominant repeated upstream cost is Upgrade fallback activity data at 80-107s (median 100s, p90 107s), while Assemble Dashboard Language site stayed at 2-5s (median 3s) and Upload dashboard artifact at 7-9s. Trusted logs for runs 36964013511 and 36965454791 also confirmed the producer still recopied a 500.7-502.5 MiB gh-aw-logs.sqlite plus 131-132 activity shards totaling 319.4-320.6 MiB into the artifact before upload. That qualifying reusable-dashboard optimization is already represented by suggestion fingerprint reusable-dashboard-skip-reupgrade-of-validated-activity-cache in repository memory, and the target repository has issues disabled, so no new non-duplicate recommendation is actionable in this cycle.

no_actionable_improvement: evaluated Astro documentation generation across the latest 20 completed successful docs.yml runs from 2026-10-01T20:49Z through 2026-10-02T01:02Z, plus comparable successful cao-dashboard.yml producer run 36942640668. Trusted Actions metadata showed 20 successful docs runs within the 14-day window, satisfying the minimum sample gate, but only 11 comparable successful build executions because 9 successful scheduled runs short-circuited after schedule-freshness and skipped build/deploy. Across all 20 successes, full workflow wall time median was 43.5s with p90 88.0s; among the 11 comparable build executions, build-job median was 48.0s with p90 53.0s, build queue median was 4.0s with p90 4.0s, deploy-job median was 20.0s with p90 33.0s on the 5 runs that actually deployed, and schedule-freshness median was 7.0s with p90 9.0s on successful scheduled runs. Build-step medians across comparable docs builds were 12.0s for Build documentation, 6.0s for Restore node_modules, 2.0s for Restore cached CAO Dashboard, and 9.0s for Upload Pages artifact; representative trusted logs and step metadata confirmed cache hits for actions/setup-node npm cache, the explicit node_modules cache, and the central-agentic-ops-dashboard cache, with Install dependencies, Save node_modules, Find latest CAO Dashboard run, and Mount latest CAO Dashboard artifact skipped on every comparable successful build. Astro documentation generation therefore remains about 25% of median docs build execution but only 12s absolute, far below the actionable threshold of saving at least 60s or 15% of median full workflow time without weakening freshness or correctness. Cross-checking successful cao-dashboard producer run 36942640668 again showed the dominant repeated upstream cost remains reusable dashboard preparation rather than Astro docs generation: Upgrade fallback activity data took 97s while Assemble Dashboard Language site took 4s and Upload dashboard artifact took 9s, and trusted logs confirmed repeated copying of a 483.8 MiB SQLite file plus 127 activity shards totaling 308.5 MiB into the artifact before upload. That larger reusable-dashboard optimization is already represented by suggestion fingerprint reusable-dashboard-skip-reupgrade-of-validated-activity-cache in repository memory and open issues #15332 and #15497, so no new non-duplicate recommendation is actionable in this Astro documentation generation cycle.
